text:
Agent: Cedar Bank, card support, Jenna speaking.
Customer: Hi, I'm in Lisbon, just trying to check in at my hotel, and the front desk says my card was declined when they tried to take the deposit. Same thing happened this morning when I tried to book my flight home online.
Agent: I'm sorry about that. Let me look at your account. Can I have your full name and the last four digits of the card?
Customer: Hannah Lowe, ending eight-eight-two-zero.
Agent: Thank you, Hannah. I can see the card has been temporarily blocked for security. There were three transactions in a row in Portugal, a hotel pre-authorization of four hundred euros, an airline payment, and a taxi, and our system flagged them because you hadn't set a travel notice.
Customer: Oh no, I forgot. I'm here for a week, for a conference.
Agent: No problem, I can lift the block right now, but I'll need to verify with a code. I'm sending a text to your registered number.
Customer: Got it. Four-six-one-three.
Agent: Perfect. The block is removed. I've also added a travel notice for Portugal until the twenty-eighth. Your daily limit abroad is two thousand euros, do you need it raised for the hotel stay?
Customer: Maybe a little. The hotel wants to hold the whole six nights, about nine hundred. And the flight is another four hundred.
Agent: That fits within the limit. Make sure the hotel retries the deposit now. Hold amounts show as pending, they'll drop off after checkout.
Customer: Great. I'll go back to the front desk. Thanks, Jenna.

metadata.note: Card blocked abroad while paying a hotel and booking flights; full of travel vocabulary (hotel, check-in, boarding) but the issue is card block and limits. Imitates travel/hotels; true topic cards.
